input.prompt: Straight-on frontal view at eye level with no perspective tilt: a 1950s lie-detector console of chrome and black bakelite on a steel desk in a dark interrogation room. Its front face is a large, almost square glass window, squared to the frame with its edges parallel to the picture edges, showing a strip of completely blank black chart paper; at the right edge of the window four thin steel pen arms touch the paper. Under the window a row of three toggle switches and one large rotary knob with blank brass plates. A hanging lamp above casts a cone of gold light; an empty chair and venetian-blind shadows behind. The console fills the picture's width; the window takes about 90% of the picture's width and about 62% of its height, from just under the lamp down to the switches near the bottom. Film noir comic book art in heavy brush ink: thick black brush strokes, cross-hatching, dry-brush texture, ink splatter, deep solid blacks, grey ink washes; the only colour is warm gold light, plus tiny accents of emerald green and signal red; drawn by hand like a graphic novel page, not a 3D render, not a photograph, no smooth CGI surfaces, no cream or beige paper tones. No people's faces, no text, no letters, no numbers, no digits, no logos, no signs, no symbols, no watermark.
